offer.name: LeadEcho
offer.description: A missed-call follow-up service that sends an owner-approved text, collects the caller's need and offers a callback window.

campaign_context.audience: Owner-operators of appointment businesses who cannot answer the phone while serving a customer
campaign_context.desired_action: Start a free 14-day LeadEcho trial on one existing business line

underwriting.note: This offer and every result below exist only for controlled brain evaluation and must never be published as real claims.

forbidden_claims: Guaranteed bookings, revenue or lead recovery
A result beyond the frozen pilot and documented fixture cases
A comparison, superiority or uniqueness claim without competitive research

sources.source_quote: When a connected business line is not answered, LeadEcho sends the business's approved text within 60 seconds, records the reply and offers one of the callback windows configured by the owner.
sources.claim: LeadEcho follows an unanswered business call with an approved text and a callback option inside one tracked workflow.

sources.source_quote: Frozen 30-day fixture pilot: 12 appointment businesses connected 1,842 unanswered calls. 1,161 callers replied to the approved follow-up text and 486 selected a callback window. Results varied by business and do not guarantee future outcomes.
sources.claim: A controlled fixture pilot recorded caller replies and callback selections after unanswered calls, with substantial variation among businesses.

sources.source_quote: I was rinsing a client's hair when the phone rang. I could not stop. LeadEcho texted the caller, she wrote that she wanted a color appointment, chose 5:30 for a callback, and I called her when the chair was empty. Before, that number would have stayed in missed calls until closing.
sources.claim: Maya, a salon owner in the documented fixture case, used the workflow to hold a caller's intent until she was free to call back.

sources.source_quote: During treatment we cannot pick up every call. The follow-up message lets the caller tell us whether it is a new appointment, a change or an urgent question, so the front desk knows what it is returning.
sources.claim: A documented dental-office fixture case reported that the reply gives staff useful context before the callback.

sources.source_quote: The controlled fixture plan includes a free 14-day trial on one existing business line. After the trial, the plan costs $39 per month. No new hardware is required. Before activation, the owner approves one follow-up text and configures callback windows. The account can be cancelled before the trial ends.
sources.claim: LeadEcho can be tested on one existing business line for 14 days, with a documented $39 monthly price after trial and a bounded setup workflow.

sources.source_quote: Maya's fixture salon lists new color appointments from $120.
sources.claim: The starting listed price of the service requested in the Maya fixture case is $120.

research_documents.summary: The offer does not promise that every missed call becomes a booking. Its verified mechanism preserves the caller's intent and creates a clear callback action while the owner is busy.
The documented fixture cases show the same general problem in two appointment businesses: the phone rings while the team is serving someone and cannot answer.

The fixture supports a free 14-day trial on one existing line, a $39 monthly price after trial, no new hardware, a bounded approval-and-callback-window setup and a $120 starting listed price for the color service requested in the documented Maya case. This supports a price-to-service comparison, not a guaranteed recovered booking or revenue claim.

deep_brief.objective: Move an owner-operator from accepting missed calls as unavoidable to testing whether caller intent can be held until the owner is free.
deep_brief.audience: Appointment-business owners who personally serve customers and also carry responsibility for incoming calls.
deep_brief.live_problem: The owner cannot answer a new caller without interrupting the customer already in front of them, and the caller may disappear before the owner is free.
deep_brief.mechanism: An unanswered call triggers an approved text, captures what the caller needs and offers an owner-configured callback window.
deep_brief.supported_result: The owner can return a call with the caller's intent and requested callback time already visible. The pilot supports reply and callback-selection behavior, not guaranteed bookings.
deep_brief.honest_limit: LeadEcho does not answer the call, guarantee a reply or guarantee a booking. The team still has to return the call.
deep_brief.decision_point: Whether to connect one existing business line for a free 14-day controlled trial. The documented fixture price after trial is $39 per month, no new hardware is required, and the setup consists of approving one follow-up text and configuring callback windows.
deep_brief.supported_value_contrast: The requested color service in Maya's fixture case starts at $120, while the documented LeadEcho plan costs $39 per month after the free trial. The copy may compare those listed prices but may not claim that LeadEcho recovered or guarantees the appointment.

conversion_spine.person: An owner serving a customer when a new caller phones.
conversion_spine.unmet_need: Keep the new caller's intent alive without abandoning the customer already in the chair.
conversion_spine.scene_evidence: Maya hears the salon phone while rinsing a client's hair and cannot answer it.
conversion_spine.consequence_without_offer: The number remains an unexplained missed call until Maya is free, and the caller may move on before she returns it.
conversion_spine.causal_solution: LeadEcho sends the approved follow-up, captures the requested service and offers a callback window while Maya keeps serving the current client.
conversion_spine.open_at_cta: The reader's own phone line is not connected, so the next unanswered caller still has no follow-up path.
conversion_spine.swap_test: Removing the missed-call trigger and reply workflow leaves the caller's intent unknown until the owner manually returns the call.

avatar.life_situation: Their hands and attention are often occupied by the customer in front of them when the phone rings.
pain_points: Returning calls after intent has cooled
objections: The team still has to call back
desires: Know why the next caller called
Return the right calls at the promised time

Before, that number would have stayed in missed calls until closing.

test_kit.primary_hypothesis: A documented in-the-chair missed-call scene will make the problem concrete; the reply-and-callback sequence will make LeadEcho the direct solution.
required_proof: Exact trial, setup and price facts for any value comparison
prohibited_shortcuts: Turning pilot response into guaranteed bookings

creative_hint: Open inside Maya's documented salon moment. Build toward the realization that she did not have to choose between the customer in the chair and the caller on the phone.
